newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees $9 bln of foreign investment in '96.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees $9 bln of foreign investment in '96.

text.p: Trade Minister Herminio Blanco on Monday said Mexico may have received some $9 billion in foreign investment in 1996, about the same level as 1995.

"In 1995, direct foreign investment reached $9 billion, and in 1996 preliminary data from the National Register of Foreign Investment leads us to expect a similar amount," he said in a ceremony attended by President Ernesto Zedillo.
Zedillo described Mexico as the developing world's second largest destination for direct foreign investment, after China, and he expected it to continue rising.

Blanco, meanwhile, predicted that exports in 1997 were likely to climb to $110 billion from some $96 billion last year. This, he said, was about 25 percent of gross domestic product, a level similar to Germany and Hong Kong.
